summary: Two pinned MLX Metal implementations expose the same source-level choreography: SIMDgroup-local reduction, lane-zero partial publication through threadgroup memory, and a second SIMDgroup reduction over those partials.
normalized_steps: Form or receive one or more per-thread FP32 values.
Reduce each value within its SIMDgroup.
Have one lane per SIMDgroup publish a partial into threadgroup storage.
Synchronize the threadgroup so the partials are visible before consumption.
Load the partial slots into SIMDgroup lanes and perform the final SIMDgroup reduction.
observed_variants: RMS normalization has SIMDgroup zero perform the final reduction, then lane zero publishes one precise inverse-root-mean scalar into threadgroup memory.
Layer normalization has every SIMDgroup perform the final reduction, templates the helper over multiple accumulators, and returns reduced values through per-thread state.
